dataPath <- "Data/"
outPath  <- "Results/"

# Helper: load an .RData object safely
load_obj <- function(f) {
  if (!file.exists(f)) return(NULL)
  e <- new.env(); load(f, envir = e); get(ls(e)[1], envir = e)
}

fmt <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)

  if (is.null(x)) NULL else data.table(Year = y, x)

  x <- load_obj(paste0(dataPath, "tacsat_", y, ".RData"))
  if (is.null(x)) NULL else data.table(Year = y, x)[, .(Year, SI_LATI, SI_LONG)]
}))

  x <- load_obj(paste0(outPath, "tacsatActivity", y, ".RData"))
  if (is.null(x)) NULL else data.table(Year = y, as.data.table(x)[, .(LE_GEAR, SI_SP, SI_STATE, SI_LATI, SI_LONG)])
}))
tef <- rbindlist(lapply(years, function(y) {
  x <- load_obj(paste0(outPath, "tacsatEflalo", y, ".RData"))
  if (is.null(x)) NULL else data.table(Year = y, as.data.table(x)[, .(VE_REF, SI_DATE, LE_GEAR, SI_LATI, SI_LONG, INTV, LE_KG_TOT)])
}))
# INTV is in minutes until step 2.5 divides it by 60 (hours); detect the unit per year
if (nrow(tef)) tef[, INTV_h := if (median(INTV, na.rm = TRUE) > 1) INTV / 60 else INTV, by = Year]
```

# Purpose and scope

This document records how the Andalusian small-scale fleet tracking data
("cajas verdes") merged with sales notes were prepared for the
ICES VMS and Logbook Data Call R workflow (ICES-VMS-and-Logbook-Data-Call,
version 2.1.0, commit `a844911`). It describes (i) the nature of the source data,
(ii) how they were transformed into the TACSAT and EFLALO exchange formats
(Annex 3 of the data call), (iii) the assumptions needed to fit them into a
workflow designed for logbook/VMS data from larger vessels, and (iv) every change
made to the ICES base scripts and why.

**Scope of this run**

* Fleets: traps and pots (**FPO**: *nasas* and *trampas*) and hydraulic
  dredges (**HMD**: *dragas mecanizadas hidráulicas*).
* Years: **2023 and 2024**.
* Area: ICES Division **27.9.a** (Gulf of Cádiz). Mediterranean activity is
  excluded (see Section 4).

# Nature of the source data

## Cajas verdes (green boxes)

The "cajas verdes" are positioning devices installed on Andalusian small-scale
vessels that are not covered by the EU VMS obligation (most are < 12 m). They
work like a high-frequency VMS:

* Positions are reported roughly **every 3 minutes** (median interval
  191 s), much more often than standard VMS (1–2 h).
* Each record includes position, instantaneous speed and heading, plus
  derived fields (speed and course computed from consecutive positions,
  distance, time difference and an in-port flag).
* Time stamps are stored in **local time (Europe/Madrid)**.

## Sales notes (notas de venta)

Landings come from first-sale notes, not from logbooks. Small-scale vessels
under 10 m are not required to keep an EU logbook, so the sales note is the only
record of the catch. Sales notes give:

* sale date, total weight (kg) and total value (EUR) per trip;
* the number of species sold, but **not the weight by species** in the
  merged file used here.

## Merged file

Both sources were merged before this work into a single ping-level table,
`Data/CV_NV_2018_2024_ZE.fst` (`r if (file.exists(paste0(dataPath, "CV_NV_2018_2024_ZE.fst"))) paste(fmt(fst::metadata_fst(paste0(dataPath, "CV_NV_2018_2024_ZE.fst"))$nrOfRows), "rows") else "about 20.3 million rows"`, 2018–2024). Each
ping carries the trip identifier and the landing totals of its trip.

```{r source-fields}
src <- data.table(
  Field = c("FT_REF", "VE_REF", "ANYO", "SI_TIMESTAMP", "SI_LATI / SI_LONG",
            "SI_SP / SI_HE", "SI_TDIFF", "EN_PUERTO", "LE_MET4", "ARTE",
            "FECHAVENTA", "TOTAL_KILOS / TOTAL_EUROS", "LE_MET6"),
  Content = c("Trip identifier = vessel + date (one trip per vessel and day)",
              "Vessel CFR code (ESP + 9 digits)",
              "Year",
              "Ping time, local time (Europe/Madrid)",
              "Position, decimal degrees",
              "Instantaneous speed (knots) and heading (degrees)",
              "Seconds since previous ping",
              "1 = ping inside a port polygon",
              "Gear, metier level 4",
              "Gear name in the national census",
              "Sale date of the trip",
              "Trip landings (kg) and value (EUR), repeated on each ping",
              "Metier level 6 (empty in this file)"))
kable(src, booktabs = TRUE, caption = "Fields of the merged source file used in this work.")
```

# Transformation to TACSAT and EFLALO

The conversion is done by `0_cajasverdes_formato.R`, which runs **before**
`0_global.R`. It reads the `.fst` file, keeps the selected fleets and years, and
writes `Data/tacsat_YYYY.RData` and `Data/eflalo_YYYY.RData`, with object names
`tacsat_YYYY` and `eflalo_YYYY`, as `1_eflalo_tacsat_preprocessing.R` expects.

## Comparison with the data call formats

Tables 2 and 3 compare each field required by the data call (Annex 3, TACSAT2
and EFLALO2 formats) with what the cajas verdes and sales notes provide.
**Status** is one of: *Direct* (field exists and is copied), *Converted* (exists
but changes unit, time zone or format), *Derived* (computed from other fields),
*Assumed* (filled by an assumption, Section 4), *Missing* (not available; left NA).

```{r cmp-tacsat}
cmpT <- data.table(
  Field    = c("VE_REF", "VE_COU", "SI_LATI", "SI_LONG", "SI_DATE", "SI_TIME", "SI_SP", "SI_HE"),
  `Data call format` = c("Vessel ID, 20 char", "ISO 3166-1 alpha-3", "Decimal degrees",
                         "Decimal degrees", "DD/MM/YYYY", "HH:MM, UTC", "Knots", "Degrees"),
  `Cajas verdes` = c("VE_REF (CFR)", "not present", "SI_LATI", "SI_LONG",
                     "SI_TIMESTAMP (POSIXct)", "SI_TIMESTAMP, Europe/Madrid, seconds",
                     "SI_SP (knots)", "SI_HE (degrees)"),
  Status = c("Direct", "Assumed (ESP)", "Direct", "Direct", "Converted",
             "Converted (UTC, minute)", "Direct", "Direct"))
kable(cmpT, booktabs = TRUE,
      caption = "TACSAT2 format required by the data call vs. cajas verdes positions.")
```

cmpA <- data.table(
  `Annex field` = c("VesselLengthRange", "AverageVesselLength / AveragekW",

**Summary.** Positions are complete and of higher resolution than standard VMS.
The main gaps are on the logbook side: vessel characteristics (length, power,
tonnage), species composition of the landings, mesh size and ports. Vessel
characteristics are the only gap that blocks required Annex fields, and they can
be filled from the EU Fleet Register by CFR.

## TACSAT (positions)

* One row per ping, restricted to trips kept in EFLALO.
* Time converted from Europe/Madrid to **UTC**, truncated to the minute
  (`SI_DATE` = dd/mm/yyyy, `SI_TIME` = HH:MM).
* When two pings of one vessel fall in the same minute, only the first is kept.
  Otherwise `intervalTacsat()` would produce zero-length intervals.
* `VE_COU` = ESP. `SI_SP` and `SI_HE` are taken directly from the device.

## EFLALO (trips and landings)

One row per trip (`FT_REF`), built from the pings of that trip:

```{r eflalo-map}
map <- data.table(
  `EFLALO field` = c("VE_REF", "VE_FLT, LE_GEAR", "VE_COU, FT_DCOU, FT_LCOU",
                     "FT_DDAT / FT_DTIME", "FT_LDAT / FT_LTIME",
                     "FT_DHAR, FT_LHAR", "LE_ID", "LE_CDAT", "LE_MET",
                     "LE_RECT", "LE_DIV", "LE_MSZ", "LE_KG_MZZ / LE_EURO_MZZ",
                     "VE_LEN, VE_KW, VE_TON"),
  Source = c("VE_REF (CFR)", "LE_MET4", "\"ESP\"",
             "First ping of the trip (UTC)", "Last ping of the trip (UTC)",
             "NA (not available)", "FT_REF + \"_1\" (one log event per trip)",
             "FECHAVENTA (sale date)",
             "FPO -> FPO_CEP_>0_0_0; HMD -> HMD_MOL_>0_0_0",
             "Most frequent ICES rectangle of the at-sea pings in 27.9.a",
             "27.9.a, or 37.1.1 if most at-sea pings have longitude > -5.6",
             "NA (passive gear / dredge)",
             "TOTAL_KILOS / TOTAL_EUROS of the trip",
             "EU Fleet Register by CFR (pending, see Section 7)"))
kable(map, booktabs = TRUE, caption = "Origin of each EFLALO field.")
```

# Assumptions

The ICES workflow was designed for EU logbook and VMS data. Using it with cajas
verdes and sales notes requires the assumptions below. They should be read
together with any product derived from these data.

1. **Trip = vessel-day.** `FT_REF` is defined as vessel + date in the source
   file. Departure and arrival are taken as the first and last ping of that
   day, not as declared port times. The median trip lasts about 21 h because the
   device keeps reporting while the vessel is in port. The workflow removes
   in-port pings (3 km harbour buffer), so effort is not inflated, but trip
   duration as such should not be interpreted.
2. **One log event per trip.** Sales notes have no haul or fishing-operation
   resolution, so each trip has a single `LE_ID`. Landings are spread over the
   fishing pings of the trip (`linkEflaloTacsat = "trip"`).
3. **Sale date = catch date.** `LE_CDAT` is the sale date. More than 99.9% of
   trips are sold on the day of the last ping.
4. **Landings not split by species.** Only trip totals are available, so all
   landings are reported under the generic FAO code **MZZ** (marine fishes
   n.e.i.). The Annex 1 (VE) and Annex 2 (LE) tables use only total weight
   and value, so the submitted totals are unaffected. Species-level outputs
   from this run must not be used.
5. **Metier level 6 assigned by gear.** `LE_MET6` is empty in the source file.
   All FPO trips are assigned `FPO_CEP_>0_0_0` (octopus pots) and all HMD trips
   `HMD_MOL_>0_0_0` (bivalve dredges). Both codes are valid in the RDB-ISSG
   metier list. FPO trips targeting other species (fish, crustaceans) are
   therefore misclassified at level 6.
6. **FPO includes *nasas* and *trampas*.** Both carry `LE_MET4 = FPO` and are
   treated as one fleet.
7. **ICES area boundary.** Trips with most at-sea pings east of 5°36'W (the FAO
   27/37 boundary at the Strait of Gibraltar) are classified as Mediterranean
   (`LE_DIV = 37.1.1`) and excluded. This removes about 83% of the FPO trips,
   which mostly operate from Mediterranean ports. The workflow also removes
   individual pings outside its ICES-area polygons.
8. **Mesh size and harbours unknown.** `LE_MSZ`, `FT_DHAR` and `FT_LHAR` are NA.
   They are not used to build the annex tables.
9. **Time zone.** All times are converted to UTC, as required by TACSAT/EFLALO.

# Issues found when moving cajas verdes data into the data call workflow

The ICES workflow assumes EU logbooks (one record per haul or fishing day, with
species-level catch, vessel details and declared ports) and EU VMS (one position
every 1–2 hours, vessels of 12 m or more). Cajas verdes and sales notes differ on
almost every one of these points. The issues below were found in this exercise.
They are grouped by stage, and for each one the consequence and the solution
adopted are stated.

## Data structure and identifiers

* **No logbook; sales notes act as EFLALO.** The fleet is not obliged to keep an
  EU logbook. Landings come from first-sale notes, which record what was sold,
  when and for how much, not where or how it was caught. The EFLALO "log event"
  (`LE_*`) fields therefore have no direct source and were built from the
  positions (rectangle, division) or by assumption (metier, catch date).
* **Trips are not declared.** There is no departure or arrival declaration. The
  trip identifier in the source file is vessel + calendar day, so `FT_DDAT/TIME`
  and `FT_LDAT/TIME` were taken from the first and last ping of the day. The
  device keeps reporting in port, so trips appear to last about 20 h and start
  around midnight. Trip duration is not meaningful. Effort is protected only
  because the workflow later removes in-port pings.
* **One log event per trip.** Without haul-level information, `LE_ID` is
  `FT_REF_1`, and landings are spread evenly over all fishing pings of the trip
  (`linkEflaloTacsat = "trip"`). Spatial allocation of landings follows the
  fishing pings, not the actual catch location.
* **Merged, ping-level source file.** The source is a single 20-million-row
  ping table in `.fst` format, with trip totals repeated on every ping. It had to
  be split into two tables (TACSAT and EFLALO) and aggregated back to one row
  per trip. `.fst` needs the `fst` package, which is not part of the workflow.
* **Object and file naming is strict.** Step 1 expects `Data/tacsat_YYYY.RData`
  and `Data/eflalo_YYYY.RData` containing objects named exactly `tacsat_YYYY` and
  `eflalo_YYYY`, one per year in `yearsToSubmit`. Any year in that vector without
  its files stops the run.

## Time and position

* **Local time instead of UTC.** Cajas verdes timestamps are in Europe/Madrid
  local time (UTC+1/+2 with daylight saving). TACSAT and EFLALO require UTC. All
  times were converted, which moves some pings and trip boundaries to the
  previous calendar day.
* **Second resolution.** TACSAT stores `HH:MM`. Truncating to the minute created
  duplicate vessel-minute pairs, which were reduced to one ping. Without that,
  `intervalTacsat()` produces zero-length intervals.
* **Reporting frequency 20–40 times higher than VMS.** Pings arrive every
  ~3 minutes. The default pseudo-duplicate threshold (`intThres = 5` min) would
  delete about 98% of the positions in step 1. It had to be lowered to 1 min.
  The higher resolution also means 10–20 times more rows than for an equivalent
  VMS fleet, with longer run times and larger memory use.
* **Pings on land and in estuaries.** 7–13% of the pings fall outside the ICES
  area polygons used in step 1: east of the Strait, but also over land, in
  marinas and in inner estuaries such as the Guadalquivir. They are removed, but
  some of them may be real activity in coastal waters that the polygons do not
  cover.
* **Long periods in port.** About 20% of the remaining pings lie within the
  3 km harbour buffer and are removed. For small vessels that fish close to
  port, the 3 km buffer may also remove some genuine fishing pings.

## Area of activity

* **Mediterranean activity mixed with Atlantic activity.** The same fleets work
  on both sides of the Strait of Gibraltar. ICES only covers FAO area 27, so trips
  with most at-sea pings east of 5°36'W were excluded. This removes about 83% of
  the FPO trips, so the FPO fleet in the data call is a small fraction of the
  real fleet.
* **Rectangles not recorded.** `LE_RECT` and `LE_DIV` are not in the sales notes.
  They were assigned from the most frequent rectangle of the at-sea pings. Trips
  that cross rectangles are attributed to only one of them in the LE table.

## Vessel characteristics

* **No vessel length, power or tonnage.** The source file has only the CFR code.
  `VE_LEN`, `VE_KW` and `VE_TON` are needed for `VesselLengthRange`,
  `AverageVesselLength`, `AveragekW`, `kWFishingHour` and `kWFishingDays`, and for
  the gear-width model. They must be joined from the EU Fleet Register by CFR,
  and the register keeps a history of events, so the record valid in each year
  must be selected. Until this is done, `VE_KW` is set to 0 by the workflow and
  kW-based effort is zero.
* **Fleet segmentation.** `VE_FLT` was set to the gear (FPO, HMD), not to a DCF
  fleet segment.

## Catch information

* **No species breakdown.** The merged sales notes give only total kg and EUR per
  trip. All landings were reported as FAO code MZZ. Annex totals are correct,
  but species-based checks are meaningless: the outlier check in step 1 and any
  species-level product.
* **Metier level 6 missing.** `LE_MET6` is empty. Metiers were assigned by gear
  (`FPO_CEP_>0_0_0`, `HMD_MOL_>0_0_0`). Without species data, FPO trips that
  target fish or crustaceans cannot be separated from octopus trips.
* **Sale date instead of catch date.** `LE_CDAT` is the sale date. It coincides
  with the trip day in more than 99.9% of trips, but not by definition.
* **Mesh size and ports unknown.** `LE_MSZ`, `FT_DHAR` and `FT_LHAR` are NA.

## Fishing activity definition

* **Automatic detection fails for hydraulic dredges.** HMD is in the default
  `autoDetectionGears`. The mixture model classified the full speed range as
  fishing (up to 22 kn in 2023 and 14 kn in 2024), although the speed
  histograms show clearly separated fishing (~1–3 kn) and steaming (~7–9 kn)
  modes. Fishing hours are overestimated and spread over transit routes unless
  fixed, gear-specific thresholds are used.
* **Passive gears were never classified as fishing (workflow bug).** For gears
  outside `autoDetectionGears` (FPO), the fixed-speed rule in step 2 never ran
  because of a typo (`LE_l5MET`) and two column mismatches. Every FPO ping was
  set to "steaming" and the fleet disappeared from the outputs. The bug was
  fixed (Section 6).
* **Speed rule is not ideal for pots.** Pot fishing is detected by speed only
  (default 1–6 kn). Hauling and setting happen at low and variable speeds, and
  pots soak unattended, so "fishing hours" for FPO measure time spent working the
  gear, not fishing time.
* **Gear width.** HMD maps to the BENTHIS metier `DRB_MOL`. Without vessel length
  the default BENTHIS width (17 m) is used for all vessels. FPO has no BENTHIS
  equivalent, so it has no swept area, which is correct for a passive gear.

## Workflow and software issues

* **Single-species EFLALO breaks step 2.** `rowSums()` on one `LE_KG_*` column
  fails because base R drops the data frame to a vector (fixed with
  `drop = FALSE`).
* **External services are required at run time.** The workflow downloads the
  metier list (GitHub), the BENTHIS gear-width table (ICES API) and the habitat
  and bathymetry layers (ICES SharePoint, 1.2 GB). During this run the
  SharePoint download was truncated without warning (no size check) and the ICES
  API returned HTTP 500. A size check and a local copy of the BENTHIS table were
  needed.
* **Missing package dependencies.** `icesVMS` failed to load because its
  dependency `sqldf` was not installed. The resulting error ("could not find
  function get_benthis_parameters") does not point to the cause.
* **Step 2 is not idempotent.** Its second loop reloads `tacsatEflalo`, divides
  `INTV` by 60 and saves over the same file. Re-running only that loop converts
  minutes to hours twice. An interrupted run leaves some years in minutes and
  others in hours, so step 2 must always be re-run in full.
* **Functions live in the session.** All helper functions (`trip_assign()`,
  `add_gearwidth()`, ...) are defined in `0_global.R`. Restarting R between
  steps produces "could not find function" errors until `0_global.R` is sourced
  again. That script also re-extracts the 1.2 GB habitat archive on every run.

# Changes to the ICES base code

The ICES scripts (`0_global.R`, `1_eflalo_tacsat_preprocessing.R`,
`2_eflalo_tacsat_analysis.R`, `3_data_submission.R`) are a community-maintained
reference implementation. They should stay as close as possible to the official
version so that results are comparable between countries and new releases can
be merged without conflicts. The repository was copied without modification
(`ORIGEN.txt`).

The few changes below were unavoidable for these data. Each one is minimal and
marked in the code with a comment, and the original value is kept in the comment.

```{r changes}
chg <- data.table(
  Location = c("0_global.R, l. 71", "0_global.R, l. 76",
               "0_global.R, add_gearwidth()",
               "2_eflalo_tacsat_analysis.R, l. 491/493",
               "2_eflalo_tacsat_analysis.R, speed rule"),
  Original = c("intThres <- 5", "yearsToSubmit <- c(2009:2025)",
               "get_benthis_parameters() only",
               "eflalo[, idx_kg]", "LE_l5MET / speedarr$LE_GEAR"),
  Changed  = c("intThres <- 1", "yearsToSubmit <- c(2023:2024)",
               "local copy if the API fails",
               "eflalo[, idx_kg, drop = FALSE]", "LE_L5MET"),
  Type = c("Setting", "Setting", "Robustness", "Bug fix", "Bug fix"))
kable(chg, booktabs = TRUE, caption = "Changes made to the ICES base scripts.")
```

**`intThres` (setting).** Pings closer in time than `intThres` minutes are
removed as pseudo-duplicates (step 1.2.4). The default of 5 min assumes VMS
reporting every 1–2 h. Cajas verdes report every ~3 min, and 98% of the
intervals are shorter than 5 min, so the default would delete almost all
positions. With 1 min only genuine duplicates are removed (one ping in 2024).

**`yearsToSubmit` (setting).** This parameter is meant to be set by each user.
Only 2023 and 2024 were prepared. With the default, step 1 stops when it cannot
find `tacsat_2009.RData`.

**`drop = FALSE` (bug fix).** Step 2 sums all `LE_KG_*` and `LE_EURO_*` columns
with `rowSums(eflalo[, idx_kg])`. When there is only one species column (here
`LE_KG_MZZ`), base R drops the data frame to a vector and `rowSums()` fails
("'x' must be an array of at least two dimensions"). Adding `drop = FALSE`
returns the same result for any number of species, so the fix does not change
the output for other users. It should be reported to the workflow maintainers
(accessions@ices.dk / WGSFD).

**Speed rule for non-automatic gears (bug fix).** Gears that are not in
`autoDetectionGears` (here FPO) are classified as fishing when their speed falls
inside a fixed range (`speedarr`). In version 2.1.0 this block had three errors:
it read `nonsubTacsat$LE_l5MET` (lower-case "l", a column that does not exist, so
the loop never ran); it looked up `speedarr$LE_GEAR` (the column is
`LE_L5MET`); and it compared the gear code with a level-5 metier. As a result
**no ping of any non-automatic gear was ever set to fishing**, and the whole FPO
fleet disappeared from the effort and landings outputs. The block now uses
`LE_L5MET` throughout, and the original lines are kept as comments. The error is
still present in the latest official commit (`a844911`, 5 October 2026) and
affects every country using passive gears, so it should be reported to the
maintainers.

**Gear width parameters (robustness).** `add_gearwidth()` downloads the BENTHIS
gear-width parameters from the ICES API (`taf.ices.dk/vms/api/gearwidths`).
During this run the server returned HTTP 500 and the step failed. A fallback was
added: if the API does not return a table, the function reads
`resources/benthis_gearwidths_sfdSAR.csv`. That file holds the same table
(14 BENTHIS metiers), extracted from the README of the ICES `sfdSAR` package. When
the API works, nothing changes. HMD maps to the BENTHIS metier `DRB_MOL`. FPO has
no BENTHIS equivalent, so it gets no gear width and no swept area, which is
correct for a passive gear.

No other line of the base code was changed. All data-specific handling is in
`0_cajasverdes_formato.R`.

# Results of pre-processing (step 1)

```{r remrecs, results = "asis"}
for (yr in years) {
  rt <- load_obj(paste0(outPath, "remrecsTacsat", yr, ".RData"))
  re <- load_obj(paste0(outPath, "remrecsEflalo", yr, ".RData"))
  if (!is.null(rt)) {
    d <- data.table(Step = rownames(rt), Rows = fmt(as.numeric(rt[, 1])),
                    `% remaining` = sub("%", "", rt[, 2]))
    print(kable(d, booktabs = TRUE, align = c("l", "r", "r"),
                caption = paste("TACSAT records remaining after each cleaning step,", yr)))
  }
  if (!is.null(re)) {
    d <- data.table(Step = rownames(re), Rows = fmt(as.numeric(re[, 1])),
                    `% remaining` = sub("%", "", re[, 2]))
    print(kable(d, booktabs = TRUE, align = c("l", "r", "r"),
                caption = paste("EFLALO records remaining after each cleaning step,", yr)))
  }
  cat("\n")
}
```

```{r fig-remrecs, fig.cap = "TACSAT records remaining after each cleaning step (step 1).", fig.height = 2.6, out.width = "75%"}
rr <- rbindlist(lapply(years, function(yr) {
  rt <- load_obj(paste0(outPath, "remrecsTacsat", yr, ".RData"))
  if (is.null(rt)) return(NULL)
  data.table(Year = factor(yr), Step = factor(rownames(rt), levels = rownames(rt)),
             Pct = as.numeric(sub("%", "", rt[, 2])))
}))
if (nrow(rr))
  ggplot(rr, aes(Step, Pct, fill = Year)) +
    geom_col(position = "dodge") +
    scale_fill_grey(start = 0.4, end = 0.75) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 100)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "% of pings remaining") +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
```

No trips were removed by the EFLALO checks: there are no duplicates, impossible
times, overlapping trips or invalid metiers. The two TACSAT losses are expected:

* **outside ICES area** (7–13%): pings east of the Strait or over land and inner
  estuaries outside the ICES polygons;
* **harbour** (about 20%): pings within 3 km of a port, where the vessels spend
  several hours a day.

# Fishing activity and effort (step 2)

`HMD` is included in the workflow's `autoDetectionGears`, so its fishing pings
are identified by fitting a mixture of normal distributions to the speed
profile. `FPO` is not in that list. It uses the fixed speed range in `speedarr`
(default 1–6 knots), which only works after the bug fix described in Section 6.

```{r speeds}
f <- paste0(outPath, "fishing_speeds_by_metier_and_year.txt")
if (file.exists(f)) {
  l <- readLines(f)
  yrs <- sub("Year: ", "", grep("^Year", l, value = TRUE))
  sp  <- grep("^\"", l, value = TRUE)
  s <- rbindlist(lapply(seq_along(sp), function(i) {
    p <- strsplit(sp[i], "\t")[[1]]
    data.table(Year = yrs[i], Metier = gsub("\"", "", p[1]),
               `Min speed (kn)` = round(as.numeric(p[2]), 2),
               `Max speed (kn)` = round(as.numeric(p[3]), 2))
  }))
  kable(unique(s), booktabs = TRUE,
        caption = "Fishing speed range of the automatic detection (HMD).")
}
```

```{r fig-speed, fig.cap = "Speed of the pings after cleaning, by gear and year, coloured by the activity state assigned in step 2 (f = fishing, s = steaming / not fishing).", fig.height = 3.6, out.width = "90%"}
if (nrow(act)) {
  ggplot(act[SI_SP <= 15], aes(SI_SP, fill = SI_STATE)) +
    geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.25, boundary = 0) +
    facet_grid(LE_GEAR ~ Year, scales = "free_y") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(f = "#2166ac", s = "grey70"), name = "State") +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
    labs(x = "Speed (knots)", y = "Pings")
}
```

```{r state-table}
if (nrow(act)) {
  st <- act[, .(Pings = .N, `Fishing (%)` = round(100 * mean(SI_STATE == "f"), 1),
                `Median fishing speed (kn)` = round(median(SI_SP[SI_STATE == "f"]), 2),
                `Max fishing speed (kn)` = if (any(SI_STATE == "f")) round(max(SI_SP[SI_STATE == "f"]), 1) else NA_real_),
            by = .(Year, Gear = LE_GEAR)][order(Year, Gear)]
  kable(st, booktabs = TRUE, caption = "Activity states assigned in step 2.")
}
```

Both gears show two clear speed modes: **fishing** at low speed (about
0.5–4 kn) and **steaming** at 6–10 kn. If the automatic detection for HMD
classifies the whole speed range as fishing (maximum fishing speed well above
4 kn in the table), fishing hours are overestimated and spread over transit
routes.

**Recommendation.** Remove `HMD` from `autoDetectionGears` in `0_global.R` and
set fixed, gear-specific ranges in `speedarr` in `2_eflalo_tacsat_analysis.R`
(after the default `speedarr$min` / `speedarr$max` lines). Base them on the
low-speed mode of the histograms and on knowledge of the fleets, for example:

```r
speedarr[speedarr$LE_L5MET == "HMD_MOL", c("min", "max")] <- c(0.5, 3)
speedarr[speedarr$LE_L5MET == "FPO_CEP", c("min", "max")] <- c(0.5, 4)
```

These values are indicative and must be checked by the fleet experts before
submission.

```{r fig-effort, fig.cap = "Fishing effort (hours) by 0.05 deg cell, gear and year, from the fishing pings with landings attached (tacsatEflalo).", fig.height = 4.6, out.width = "95%"}
if (nrow(tef)) {
  d <- tef[, .(Hours = sum(INTV_h, na.rm = TRUE)),
           by = .(Year, LE_GEAR, lon = floor(SI_LONG / 0.05) * 0.05 + 0.025,
                  lat = floor(SI_LATI / 0.05) * 0.05 + 0.025)]
  base_map(xlim = c(-7.6, -5.9), ylim = c(36.5, 37.3)) +
    geom_tile(data = d, aes(lon, lat, fill = Hours)) +
    facet_grid(LE_GEAR ~ Year) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(trans = "log10", option = "magma", direction = -1,
                         name = "Fishing hours", labels = scales::comma)
}
```

```{r fig-landmap, fig.cap = "Landings (t) distributed over fishing pings, by 0.05 deg cell, gear and year.", fig.height = 4.6, out.width = "95%"}
if (nrow(tef)) {
  d <- tef[, .(Tonnes = sum(LE_KG_TOT, na.rm = TRUE) / 1000),
           by = .(Year, LE_GEAR, lon = floor(SI_LONG / 0.05) * 0.05 + 0.025,
                  lat = floor(SI_LATI / 0.05) * 0.05 + 0.025)]
  base_map(xlim = c(-7.6, -5.9), ylim = c(36.5, 37.3)) +
    geom_tile(data = d[Tonnes > 0], aes(lon, lat, fill = Tonnes)) +
    facet_grid(LE_GEAR ~ Year) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(trans = "log10", name = "Landings (t)", labels = scales::comma)
}
```

```{r effort-table}
if (nrow(tef)) {
  et <- tef[, .(`Fishing pings` = fmt(.N), Vessels = uniqueN(VE_REF),
                `Fishing days` = fmt(uniqueN(paste(VE_REF, SI_DATE))),
                `Fishing hours` = fmt(round(sum(INTV_h, na.rm = TRUE))),
                `Hours per day` = round(sum(INTV_h, na.rm = TRUE) / uniqueN(paste(VE_REF, SI_DATE)), 1),
                `Landings (t)` = fmt(round(sum(LE_KG_TOT, na.rm = TRUE) / 1000, 1))),
            by = .(Year, Gear = LE_GEAR)][order(Year, Gear)]
  kable(et, booktabs = TRUE, align = c("l", "l", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r"),
        caption = "Effort and landings in tacsatEflalo (input to the Annex 1 table).")
}
```

# Pending issues before submission

1. **Vessel characteristics.** `VE_LEN`, `VE_KW` and `VE_TON` are still NA.
   Without them `VesselLengthRange`, `AverageVesselLength`, `AveragekW`,
   `kWFishingHour` and `kWFishingDays` cannot be computed. To fill them, export
   the EU Fleet Register for Spain to `Data/EU_fleet_register_ESP.csv`
   (matched by CFR) and re-run `0_cajasverdes_formato.R`.
2. **Fishing speed thresholds.** Apply and justify the gear-specific
   `speedarr` ranges (Section 8).
3. **Species composition.** If sales notes by species become available,
   replace `LE_KG_MZZ` with real FAO codes. Only the species columns change.
4. **Metier level 6.** If target species are available, refine
   `FPO_CEP_>0_0_0` for trips not targeting octopus.

# Reproducibility

Run from the project root, in this order:

1. `0_cajasverdes_formato.R`: source `.fst` to TACSAT/EFLALO (Annex 3).
2. `0_global.R`: settings, packages, habitat and bathymetry layers.
3. `1_eflalo_tacsat_preprocessing.R`: cleaning.
4. `2_eflalo_tacsat_analysis.R`: merging, activity, effort.
5. `3_data_submission.R`: Annex 1 (VE) and Annex 2 (LE) tables in `Results/`.

Required packages for the conversion: `fst`, `data.table`.

```{r session}
cat("R:", R.version.string, "\n")
```
